summary: Feed s158_double to IDS is degraded: 25.5% of frames are sliced to 128 bytes preventing payload inspection (high) and 15.6% are duplicates (medium). IDS requires full payload and will have severely reduced detection coverage until slicing is disabled and deduplication is enabled.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker packet slicing/truncation is enabled and cutting frames to ~128 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or fit the 1Gbps tool port. This strips L4 payload and is incompatible with IDS requirements.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection. With 959/3765 frames (25.5%) truncated, payload-based signatures, file extraction, and exploit detection will fail - traffic appears as false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: IDS is configured as needs_full_payload=true. Disable slicing on the broker policy for this IDS feed to forward full 1518-byte frames so signatures can match.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice (586/3765 = 15.6% duplicates, threshold 5%). Typical cause is aggregating the same SPAN/mirror from two directions or two TAPs without broker deduplication, or a looped broker mesh forwarding both copies to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/storage processing duplicates, inflates flow counts and alerts, skews analytics, and can cause TCP reassembly/state issues. At 15.6% it reduces effective capacity of the 1Gbps IDS port.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (de-duplication window ~10ms) on the feed to s158_double to drop the second copy before delivery to the IDS, restoring accurate traffic counts.
